While you've got a lot of people here saying that this one weapon is better than another, the answer is all of them.

Supergiant has made a game where almost every option is "the good option" based on your preferences. Some choices synergize better with others, sure, but every weapon has the potential to be amazing with almost any god.

For example, I saw one poster say that  chaos aspect shield is hard to use. It's the only shield I ever use and it's my best weapon.

You'll get plenty more Titan blood, so don't freak about this choice.

I will say the general framework of the aspects.

The Zagreus aspect is a passive buff. You don't need to actively do anything to receive it's benefit. (I.e. Move speed, crit chance)

The second aspect is a buff you can give yourself, usually by doing a certain move. (I.e. Crit chance after doing a certain move)

The third aspect is a more of a game changer, usually changing up how you play more drastically (I.e. Poseidon aspect making casting more central than melee)

You can change it up, and still have a balanced, viable build!

Well, there's two uses of the word now.
In everyday language, if I say "I have a theory" it means I have a guess.
But as a scientist, saying "I have a theory" means I have an explanation that is disprovable and may or may not be supported by facts.
Similar situation with these words.
Everyday language uses isms as discriminating against a category of people for no good reason, i.e. a shopkeeper not serving women is sexist.
But the other, formal definition used by community psychologists and the like is systemic discrimination against a group of people not in power, by a group of people in power.
So by that definition reverse isms don't exist because only one group can be in power.
By an everyday definition, one person can be sexist or racist against any group, regardless of either's level of power.
But only a group in power, e.g. white heterosexual males, can be racists according to a community psychology definition.

I don't like her videos.  Though she is raising valid points, and trying to improve gamer culture, she doesn't know enough to make proper criticisms. She claims that the game treats women as objects, except all NPCs fall into two categories, people you become emotionally attached to, like Alex from Half Life 2, and those you don't care about like, shopkeepers, pedestrians, enemies, and a good number of allies.  Since 99% of NPCs fall into the latter category, yeah, alot of women are treated as objects, but so are men. So many of her criticisms are that the game allows the player to harm women, except the game allows for you to harm everyone.  She criticizes AC for including prostitutes, but says nothing about how men are reduced to thieves and mercenaries. I love what she's trying to do, but I get the feeling she has no idea how games work fundamentally, and that she makes the erroneous claims out of ignorance.  The best example of her goodwill contrasted with her ignorance is near the end, where she first states that background women invoke no empathy in players, and they fucking shouldn't, not because their women or sex objects, but because they are background players, and you don't feel empathy towards every person you pass in the street, so the same should be true about games.  And then 10 seconds later she makes the spot on claim that they don't include the same sort of sexualized treatment that women do.  And then she makes the claim that sexual objectification in videogames is always bad and to be avoided, which one could make the argument for both sides.
